title: 3-year-old boy with vomiting
arrival: A 3-year-old boy is brought in by his father with vomiting since yesterday.
feedbackWhy: He has vomited everything he has been given since yesterday, which meets a yellow Circulation criterion. No red criterion is met. His heart rate is also above the high-risk threshold for his age, but the card is worked in order and a yellow criterion is met first, so the category is yellow.
reviewNote: CLINICIAN REVIEW REQUIRED: this case teaches that a yellow criterion decides even when a high-risk vital sign is also present (the card reaches vital signs only after a No at yellow). Confirm this is the intended teaching and that the wording is right. HR 164 is above 160 for 1-4 years. Confirm 'takes sips of water' does not count as drinking poorly. Every value is proposed.

design.intendedChallenge: A yellow criterion decides the category when it is met, even if a high-risk vital sign is also present. The vital signs step is reached only when no red or yellow criterion is met.
design.expectedCommonError: triaging as up-triage because the heart rate is above the age threshold, or as red because the heart rate is high.

airway_red.text: No stridor. No chest indrawing. No central cyanosis.

circulation_red.text: Pulse strong. Extremities warm. Capillary refill 2 seconds. No bleeding. Awake and interacting. Eyes not sunken. Skin pinch returns at once. Takes sips of water when offered.

disability_red.text: No convulsions. Awake and interacting. Not confused, restless or irritable. No stiff neck.

other_red.text: No trauma, poisoning, threatened limb, snake bite or scrotal pain.

airway_yellow.text: No swelling of the mouth, throat or neck. No wheezing.

circulation_yellow.text: Has vomited everything he has been given since yesterday. No diarrhoea. Not pale.

disability_yellow.text: Awake and interacting. Not restless or irritable. No severe pain.

other_yellow.text: No visible wasting. No swelling of both feet. No rash. No trauma. No known surgical diagnosis.
